title: Impact of Impending Winding Down of Jobs Support Scheme on Retrenchment and Unemployment
what_it_is: Impact of Impending Winding Down of Jobs Support Scheme on Retrenchment and Unemployment

sections.label: Aviation and tourism sector support
sections.summary: Aviation and tourism recovery is expected to remain weak, with support packages, vouchers and the Jobs Growth Incentive available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As such, the recovery of the aviation- and tourism-related sectors is expected to remain weak.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Transport introduced the $870 million OneAviation Support Package in February this year to enable aviation companies to preserve core capabilities and maintain Singapore’s position as an aviation hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Singapore Tourism Board launched a domestic tourism campaign and extended $320 million worth of SingapoRediscovers Vouchers to drive domestic tourism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For firms in these sectors that are still able to expand local hiring, they can also tap on the Jobs Growth Incentive, which provides up to $54,000 per hire.

sections.label: Aviation growth sectors identified
sections.summary: EDB and component agencies worked with the Emerging Stronger Task Force and Alliances for Action to identify core aviation growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In terms of the reduction in manpower requirements, EDB and the different component agencies have worked with the Emerging Stronger Task Force and also leveraging on the Singapore Together Alliances for Action (AfAs), and identified certain core sectors within the aviation industry which they think would continue to remain very much the growth sectors; the exact details I am not at liberty to talk about at this particular Sitting.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive transition support
sections.summary: Companies are urged to tap the Jobs Growth Incentive, which subsidises up to $54,000 per hire depending on the worker.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With regard to the third clarification on what kind of transition support, we urge all companies, particularly companies that are doing well, to tap on the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) which subsidises up to $54,000 per hire, depending on which age group you are, whether you are 40 years old and above, whether you have disabilities or you are an ex-offender; and also, for the young ones, where up to 25% of the monthly salary is subsidised, capped at a certain amount.

sections.label: JGI expiry date
sections.summary: The JGI scheme will expire in September 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The JGI scheme will expire in September 2021.

sections.label: Courses expanded for growth sectors
sections.summary: Courses are being expanded so graduates from Institutes of Higher Learning, polytechnics and ITE can be placed in growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we are now doing is that we are expanding the courses to ensure that the graduates coming out from the Institutes of Higher Learning, the polytechnics, the Institute of Technical Education can be placed in sectors which we have identified as growth sectors, for instance, in wholesale trade, healthcare, finance and infocomm.
